newsitem.title: USA: Missouri wheat yields reported well above average.
newsitem.headline: Missouri wheat yields reported well above average.

text.p: Missouri's winter wheat yields were generally reported to be well above average this year, according to the Missouri Agricultural Statistics Service weekly report.

Fifty-four percent of the wheat crop in Missouri had been harvested as of Sunday, three days behind last year but in line with the five-year average. The southern third of the state was most advanced with 92 percent harvested.
Double crop soybeans were 56 percent planted, two days behind the five-year average of 62 percent. A total of 95 percent of all intended soybean acres had been planted.
Eight percent of soybeans were blooming, two days ahead of the average of seven percent. Soybeans were rated 60 percent good or excellent, down from 66 percent a week earlier.
Corn condition was similar to last week at 72 percent good or excellent. Sixteen percent of the corn crop was silking, in line with the average.
Topsoil moisture was rated nine percent surplus, 73 percent adequate, 17 percent short and one percent very short.
